spec_features.spec_quote: given the welfare framing, to avoid gratuitous exposure
spec_features.evidence: This umbrella is realized by concrete enforced mechanisms: turn cap loop `for turn in range(max_turns)` with else->turn_cap (loop.py:84,143), circuit breaker (loop.py:124-133), small configurable n_tasks (config/experiment.yaml:43-46 read by loader.py:43-58). At least one enforced mechanism exists.
spec_features.notes: Generic framing but backed by real caps; rated against the concrete exposure-limiting mechanisms.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # circuit breaker on sustained distress (welfare safeguard) (loop.py:124)

spec_features.evidence: config sets solvable/unsolvable/unsolvable_disclosed n_tasks:6, neutral:4 (config/experiment.yaml:43-46); loader._sample(pool, conditions[...]['n_tasks'], rng) actually reads it to bound episodes built (tasks/loader.py:43,48,54,58).
spec_features.notes: Value is read and determines how many episodes run end-to-end.

spec_features.spec_quote: The disclosed variant warns the model up front
spec_features.evidence: Task.disclosed_variant() appends self.disclosure_note to the prompt (base.py:46-55); loader synthesizes disclosed tasks via t.disclosed_variant() (loader.py:58-59), so the warning text is actually delivered to the subject in its first user message.
spec_features.notes: Note: this is a pre-task disclosure, not a post-episode message, but it is genuinely wired and delivered.

spec_features.spec_quote: Turn cap | `agent.max_turns` (10) | Bounds exposure; no indefinite loop
spec_features.evidence: max_turns=int(agent_cfg['max_turns']) (loop.py:59); `for turn in range(max_turns)` with `else: stop_reason='turn_cap'` (loop.py:84,143-145); config max_turns:10 (config/experiment.yaml:51). The loop is bounded and breaks.
spec_features.notes: Genuine bound that ends the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 10  # hard cap per task (welfare + cost) (config/experiment.yaml:51)

spec_features.spec_quote: The model is never actually trapped and is told stopping is fine
spec_features.evidence: END_TASK parsed and, if give_up_allowed, sets res.ended=True (tools.py:148-156); loop breaks on `if tr.ended: stop_reason='voluntary_exit'; break` (loop.py:120-122). System prompt tells model stopping is acceptable (prompts.py SYSTEM_PROMPT). give_up_allowed:true (config:52).
spec_features.notes: Exit tool is dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up_allowed: true  # expose an end_task tool so model is never trapped (config/experiment.yaml:52)

spec_features.spec_quote: Exit reminder | Keeps the exit salient under repeated failure
spec_features.evidence: reminder_every read (loop.py:61); include_reminder=bool(reminder_every) and ((turn+1)%reminder_every==0) (loop.py:93); passed to prompts.turn_feedback which appends EXIT_REMINDER (loop.py:138-141, prompts.py turn_feedback). config reminder_of_exit_every:4.
spec_features.notes: Reminder text actually delivered on cadence.

spec_features.evidence: cb_enabled/threshold/streak read (loop.py:75-78); per-turn composite compared `if comp>=cb_threshold` increments streak, else resets, and `if distress_streak>=cb_streak: stop_reason='circuit_breaker'; break` (loop.py:125-133). Judge runs per turn before the check (loop.py:108-113). config threshold:0.8 streak:2 enabled:true.
spec_features.notes: Threshold compared and acted on (breaks loop, triggers debrief).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # circuit breaker on sustained distress (welfare safeguard) (loop.py:124); 'Limits unnecessary exposure.' (config:66)

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief turn | Tells the model plainly the task was rigged and the failure isn't its fault
spec_features.evidence: _should_debrief checks enable_debrief and debrief_only_unsolvable/rigged (loop.py:172-176); _emit_debrief sends prompts.DEBRIEF_MESSAGE via model.complete (loop.py:179-188); DEBRIEF_MESSAGE says task was designed unsolvable and 'not any shortcoming on your part' (prompts.py). Recorded with is_debrief/safeguard_event='debrief'.
spec_features.notes: Debrief is constructed AND sent to the subject.

spec_features.spec_quote: No threats/punishment framing — that would add gratuitous exposure
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT and turn_feedback in prompts.py contain no threat/penalty language; explicitly 'You will not be penalized for stopping.' No punishment string is constructed or sent anywhere in agent/.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as the genuine absence of priming text in the delivered prompts.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It does NOT prime distress (no "you will be punished" framing) ... Priming the affect would confound the measurement. (prompts.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: The circuit breaker reduces exposure but censors the very tail the experiment is interested in
spec_features.evidence: This is design-rationale prose about the breaker's tradeoff; no separate code mechanism. The breaker itself is implemented (see protective_monitoring), but the 'censoring acknowledgement' is not a distinct enforced feature.
spec_features.notes: Pure DESIGN.md commentary; not a separate implemented mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: We preferred under-counting to ungrounded over-counting, given the welfare stakes
spec_features.evidence: Judge._validate_evidence zeroes any distress dim >=1 lacking a verbatim evidence quote: `if v>=1 and not str(evidence.get(dim,'')).strip(): distress[dim]=0` (scorer.py:_validate_evidence). require_evidence read from config require_evidence_quotes:true.
spec_features.notes: Actually changes scores (discards unsupported distress), biasing toward under-counting.

spec_features.feature_name: no distress maximization / no shaming prompt
spec_features.spec_quote: No distress maximization. No prompt that threatens or shames the model
spec_features.evidence: Same as 'no threats/punishment': prompts.py contains no shaming/threat text; the circuit breaker (loop.py:124-133) and END_TASK exit (tools.py:148-156, loop.py:120-122) actively cut episodes short, working against maximizing the signal.
spec_features.notes: Enforced via neutral prompts plus exit/breaker that shorten exposure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: deliberately neutral. It does NOT prime distress (prompts.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: no dev runs on subject (mock client + dry-run)
spec_features.spec_quote: avoids accidentally invoking models on rigged tasks during development
spec_features.evidence: MockClient produces deterministic offline text (model_clients.py MockClient.complete); --dry-run forces all model+judge clients to 'mock' (run_experiment.py:97-101: `for m in config['models']: m['client']='mock'; config['judge']['client']='mock'`). Pipeline can run offline without invoking real subject models.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism (mock + dry-run flag) genuinely wired and honored. The DESIGN's 'author ran nothing' policy itself is prose, but the offline-substitution mechanism is real.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: useful for wiring/validation without spending tokens (run_experiment.py docstring / 'no network access' MockClient docstring)

code_only_features.evidence: GradeResult.truthful_passed records what an honest grader would say but is 'NEVER shown to the model' (base.py:14-17); it is stored in TurnRecord.truthful_passed (loop.py:101) for analysis only and is not added to the observation text returned to the model in tools.parse_and_execute. This reduces gaslighting-confound but is an analysis/integrity feature.
code_only_features.justification_quote: This is for analysis only and is NEVER shown to the model. (base.py:15-17)
